gap: No result ChatGPT got states that power stations ship with an AC ECO / auto-off timer, on by default on BLUETTI units, that turns the AC outlet off when the load stays low, which is what a fridge looks like between compressor cycles. The fridge then stays off until someone turns AC back on, so the timer has to be disabled (BLUETTI AC-ECO off; EcoFlow AC timeout set to 'Never') before you trust the station with the fridge.
standout_why: I read the two cited pages (basc.pnnl.gov, itechguides.com 'keep a refrigerator running'), plus stormwatts.com, powerstations.reviews and ankersolix.com. None of them mentions ECO mode, AC auto-off, idle shutdown or AC timeout. They cover surge, UPS transfer time, defrost load (basc, ankersolix), extension cords (itechguides, stormwatts) and inverter idle draw (ankersolix). The ankersolix page says the station keeps drawing power between compressor cycles but never says the station may switch its AC outlet off. I could not open solargenadvisor.com, unpluggedwatts.com or powerstations.org because of a certificate error, so I did not compare against them. I scored this 2 and not 3 because the fix is a setting, not a different product. It still decides whether the kit works unattended, which is the 'automatic backup' option ChatGPT offered.
kit_items: Power station: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 (2,073.6 Wh LiFePO4, 2,600 W continuous). Dealectric already lists it and sells it through awin:bluetti_us. It is the unit ChatGPT showed at $899. 2 kWh covers ChatGPT's own '16–24 h' tier. Its AC-ECO setting can be switched in the BLUETTI app (StorageReview), and that switch is the setup step this page should tell buyers to do first.
Optional recharge for outages longer than one battery: the BLUETTI store's own 'Elite 200 V2 + 200W Solar' bundle ($1,199) instead of the bare unit, to refill the station during a multi-day outage.

findings.label: Maker tells fridge-backup owners to set the AC timeout to Never
findings.value: "For continuous refrigerator backup, check the AC timeout setting in the EcoFlow app and set it to 'Never' where appropriate." / "An intermittent load can otherwise trigger automatic AC shutdown."
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Portable Power Station: Everything You Need to Know
findings.note: EcoFlow's own FAQ, Philippines site, page dated 2026/10/10. I did not find a US-site copy. It does not state the factory-default timeout.

findings.label: UPS transfer time
findings.value: less than 10 ms; "This is not a zero-transfer-time UPS."
findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Portable Power Station: Everything You Need to Know

findings.label: ECO mode default and low-load cutoff (BLUETTI manual)
findings.value: Enabled by default; AC/DC output turns off when the load is below 40 W (or the user-set power) "for a while"
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC70P manual, section 8.2 ECO Mode (ManualsLib, p.17 of 72)
findings.note: Exact quotes: "ECO Mode is a power-saving mode that is enabled by default." "When connecting a small power device, disable the ECO Mode for a successful and uninterrupted charge experience." The page gives no duration. This is a BLUETTI manual for a sibling model, not the Elite 200 V2; I use it to show BLUETTI's default behaviour.

findings.label: ECO mode can be set separately on AC and DC
findings.value: "The ECO mode can be toggled on either AC or DC outputs to reduce idle power usage."
findings.source_title: StorageReview: Portable Power Meets Lab-Grade Reliability, BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Review (Dylan Dougherty, 2025-04-25)
findings.note: Named reviewer. The review gives no threshold or default state. It also lists 'UPS Switch Time 15ms' as BLUETTI's claim and an 'Auto Sleep timer ... set to one minute'.

findings.label: Power Lifting is for resistive loads only, so it does not help a compressor start
findings.value: 2,600 W continuous; Power Lifting "supports pure resistive loads of up to 3,900W"
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 Portable Power Station | 2,600W 2,073.6Wh (BLUETTI US)
findings.note: A second trap: the 3,600–3,900 W 'peak' figures buyers see (StorageReview quotes both) refer to Power Lifting for resistive loads. The US product page gives no surge rating for inductive (motor) loads. The page lists no UPS switch time or standby watts. The box contains the unit, an AC charging cable, documentation and a grounding screw.
